I'm one of those rare birds who lives by this adage: "Don't tell me. Show me!"  When I tell you there's never been another guitarist like Gary Moore, I can easily show you that fact. Indeed, there have been some greats, several mentioned in the above Top Ten.  But this man was capable of injecting and intertwining numerous forms of music into his solos, and he did it with ease. He studied all forms of music, with a foundation in the classical, began his career as a rockster, and moved to his and the favorite of hundreds of famous musicians: the Blues.  Just watch his hands. You've never seen anything like them. Listen to him intertwine classical, blues, jazz, and rock into "The Messiah Will Come Again."  “The Messiah Will Come Again” Originally written and sung by Roy Buchanan (1939-1988), this is Moore’s amazingly innovative version; places him exactly where he ought to be: the greatest ever. http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7k07j7LcLqw  “Parisian Walkways” 9:00 http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vkUpfw4Hf3w  “Still Got the Blues” 6:00 http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4O_YMLDvvnw   “Separate Ways,” by Gary Moore, 1992 (12:00) https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aW9hCIiZ-gE&nohtml5=False
